deeper.title: What the price assumes
deeper.text: The price assumes about -1% a year growth in free cash flow for 10 years, then 3% (discount rate 10.0% = 10-year Treasury 5.0% + 5%; base: last 12 months of free cash flow). For comparison, sales grew 250% last year; 105%/yr over 3 years — the market expects a slowdown from its recent pace.

deeper.title: Return on capital
deeper.text: 87% (3 years ago -10%, rising) — each $100 invested in the business (debt + equity, net of cash) earns about $87 a year after tax; return on shareholders' equity 61% (3 years ago -13%).

deeper.title: Signed future revenue
deeper.text: Signed but not yet delivered (remaining performance obligations): $134.0B — about 1.0× the last 12 months of sales; customer prepayments not yet earned (deferred revenue): $13.0B, up from $169M a year ago.

deeper.title: Multi-year view
deeper.text: Sales grew 105%/yr over 3 years and 37%/yr over 5 years; operating margin today 75% vs a 5-year range of -41–75% (median 24%): near the top of its range (cycle peak risk: margins this high often fall back).
deeper.margin_position: near the top of its range (cycle peak risk: margins this high often fall back)

deeper.title: Cash returned to shareholders
deeper.text: Returned $1.3B to shareholders over the last 12 months ($650M buybacks + $610M dividends) = 0.2% of the company's market value. Share count up 1.8% from a year ago (stock pay outpacing buybacks — dilution).

deeper.title: Analyst estimates
deeper.text: Next year's earnings-per-share estimate $208.83, up 22% in 90 days (up 1% in the last 30); 3 analysts raised, 1 cut in 30 days. This year's earnings-per-share estimate $176.67, up 13% in 90 days; 1 analyst raised, 0 cut in 30 days. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

summary.thesis: Micron is a grade A business on a trailing P/E of 8.0, but its 74.59% operating margin is at a 5-year peak, and the price now assumes cash flow will shrink.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait, and buy only at the 471.0 support. Swing: no trade before the 2026-12-17 report.
summary.act_at: buy at 471.0; return to hold on a close above 658.73

note.happening: MU fell 13.89% in one day to 594.51, from 690.44. It closed below yesterday's 643.69 support floor, and that old support zone (now 643.27–658.73) has become resistance. None of the news in DATA explains the drop, and the next earnings report is on 2026-12-17.
note.business: Nothing in DATA shows the business changed today. The latest quarter ended 2026-09-03 and was filed 2026-10-09. It showed trailing revenue of 133.2B, up from 37.4B, and free cash flow of 59.0B, up from 1.7B. The gross margin was 80.72% and the operating margin 74.59%, up from 26.14%. The balance sheet is not at risk: Micron has 38.4B of cash against 2.8B of debt, so its net cash is 40.6B. Share dilution is small at 1.78% a year. The main business risk is the margin. The filings say the 75% operating margin sits at the top of a 5-year range that runs from -41% to 75%, and peaks like that usually fade. Memory is a cyclical business where prices swing with supply and demand (general knowledge). Today's 13.89% fall changes the price and the mood, not the reported numbers. It can still be a sign that the market expects the margin to fade before the 2026-12-17 report shows it. DATA has no segment breakdown and no analyst estimates, so demand by end market cannot be checked here.

worth.text: No discounted cash flow (DCF) value is given. A DCF values a company on its future cash, but free cash flow jumped from 1.7B to 59.0B in one year, and a jump like that can't simply be projected forward. Two other methods are left. First, the stock's own history: at its usual 5-year price-to-sales levels, the share is worth 322.32 (low), 490.66 (middle) or 833.11 (high). Second, a cash-flow sketch with a 10.1% discount rate: if free cash flow just holds flat, the share is worth 706.64. The price of 594.51 implies free cash flow starting to shrink by 4.4% a year. The gap between the methods comes down to one assumption: does today's peak margin last? The own-history method assumes it returns to normal. The cash-flow method assumes it mostly holds. If the operating margin falls to 37% with 20% starting growth, the value is 783.05, but that case needs the growth to show up. One quirk: the valuation summary in DATA still quotes yesterday's 690.44 price. My fair-value range runs from the own-history middle, 490.66, to the zero-growth value, 706.64.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow stays near 59.0B instead of shrinking as the 74.59% operating margin fades from the top of its 5-year range.
